country.match: Match each ship to the country it sailed for.
country.odd: Three of these ships sailed for {value}. Which one didn't?
country.all: Tap all {n} ships that sailed for {value}.

rows.label: Titanic
rows.description: British transatlantic passenger liner, launched and foundered in 1912
rows.hook: struck an iceberg on her maiden voyage and sank with about 1,500 lives lost

rows.label: SS Edmund Fitzgerald
rows.hook: sank with all 29 crew aboard in a storm on Lake Superior

rows.label: Mayflower
rows.description: sailing ship carrying English and Dutch Pilgrims from England to North America
rows.hook: carried the Pilgrims across the Atlantic to the New World

rows.label: HMS Victory
rows.hook: was Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar and is still in commission as the oldest of its kind

rows.label: Yamato
rows.hook: carried the largest guns ever mounted on any warship

rows.label: Bismarck
rows.hook: was a giant Nazi-era vessel named after a famous chancellor

rows.label: Britannic
rows.description: Olympic-class ocean liner. Sister ship of RMS Olympic and RMS Titanic
rows.hook: was the younger sister of Titanic and sank in the Aegean Sea during the First World War

rows.label: Lusitania
rows.description: British ocean liner sunk by a German submarine in World War I
rows.hook: was torpedoed by a German U-boat in the First World War, turning American opinion against Germany

rows.label: Queen Mary
rows.hook: is now a hotel and museum moored in Long Beach, California

rows.label: Olympic
rows.description: lead ship of the Olympic-Class ocean liners. Sister ship to RMS Titanic and HMHS Britannic
rows.hook: was the older sister of Titanic and served as a troopship in the First World War

rows.label: Andrea Doria
rows.hook: sank after colliding with another vessel in thick fog, with most aboard rescued

rows.label: USS Missouri
rows.hook: hosted the signing of the Japanese surrender that ended World War II

rows.label: Carpathia
rows.description: British ocean liner known for rescuing survivors of the RMS Titanic
rows.hook: raced through ice fields to rescue over 700 survivors of Titanic

rows.label: USS Constitution
rows.description: 1797 heavy frigate of the United States Navy, oldest commissioned naval vessel afloat
rows.hook: is nicknamed Old Ironsides and is the oldest commissioned vessel still afloat

rows.label: USS Arizona
rows.hook: sank in the attack on Pearl Harbor and now lies beneath a memorial there

rows.label: Tirpitz
rows.hook: was the second of two huge battleships, named for the architect of the Kaiser's navy

rows.label: Queen Elizabeth 2
rows.description: former ocean liner and cruise ship from the United Kingdom
rows.hook: sailed for Cunard across the Atlantic and on cruises for decades before becoming a hotel in Dubai

rows.label: Cutty Sark
rows.hook: was one of the last and fastest ships built to haul tea, named for a witch in a Burns poem

rows.label: SS Great Britain
rows.description: 1843 passenger steamship and museum in Bristol, United Kingdom
rows.hook: was designed by Brunel as the first large ship to combine an iron hull with a screw propeller

rows.label: USS Nautilus
rows.hook: was the world's first nuclear-powered boat and the first to pass beneath the North Pole

rows.label: Mary Rose
rows.hook: was a flagship of Henry VIII that sank in the Solent while fighting a French invasion fleet

rows.label: USS Maine
rows.description: second-class battleship of the United States Navy

rows.label: HMS Bounty
rows.hook: was the scene of a famous mutiny led by Fletcher Christian against Captain Bligh

rows.label: Normandie
rows.hook: was the largest and fastest passenger ship afloat when she entered service, setting an Atlantic record

rows.label: Santa Maria
rows.hook: was the largest of the three ships Columbus sailed across the Atlantic on his first voyage

rows.label: Golden Hind
rows.description: 1577 galleon, flagship of Francis Drake's circumnavigation
rows.hook: carried Francis Drake on his voyage around the world

rows.label: USS Monitor
rows.description: 1862 unique ironclad; first in United States Navy service
